items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bloom Energy Corporation alleging the company made false statements about its supply chain by failing to disclose that scandium, a critical material for its fuel cells, was sourced from China through intermediaries. The allegations emerged after a July 8, 2026 Hunterbrook Media report exposed multiple China-linked supply routes, causing Bloom Energy's stock to fall nearly 6%.

items.title: DLTR Lifts 2026 Earnings Outlook as Tariff Refunds Fund Reinvestment
items.summary: Dollar Tree raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.70-$8.05, with approximately 60 cents of benefit from tariff refunds. The company plans to reinvest about $210 million of the $383 million tariff refunds received into pricing, marketing, and store operations rather than treating it as a windfall. Q2 results showed net sales increased 7% to $4.89 billion with comparable-store sales rising 3.7%, while the company maintained its full-year sales guidance of $20.5-$20.7 billion.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition during the period of February 12, 2026 to August 5, 2026. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: 3 Reasons to Hold Alibaba Stock Despite Its High Premium P/S
items.summary: Alibaba trades at a premium valuation but offers fundamental support for existing shareholders to hold. The company's cloud and AI businesses are accelerating with AI revenues exceeding one-third of cloud sales, core e-commerce remains resilient to fund AI ambitions, and management has outlined a disciplined multi-year AI infrastructure payback plan. While near-term margin pressure from capex and quick commerce losses persists, consensus earnings growth of 76.61% for fiscal 2027 supports patience through the current investment cycle.

items.summary: RTX's $289 billion backlog is expected to grow significantly, potentially reaching $460.5 billion by 2028. items.title: Anthropic IPO: 1 Key Lesson Investors Can Learn From SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX's IPO experienced significant volatility after investors grew concerned about the company's massive AI spending ($28.5B capex with 86% going to AI infrastructure) despite modest revenue ($12.5B). Historical data shows large IPOs average only 3.5% returns over 12 months despite strong first-week gains. The article warns that Anthropic's upcoming IPO could face similar investor skepticism regarding heavy AI infrastructure spending, suggesting investors should wait rather than buy at IPO launch.

items.title: Warren Buffett Watched Alphabet's Stock Price Climb 9,000% Before He Decided to Invest. Here's Why He and Greg Abel Are Making It One of Berkshire Hathaway's Biggest Investments Now.
items.summary: Warren Buffett admitted to missing out on a 9,000% gain by not investing in Alphabet earlier, citing his historical avoidance of IPOs and tech stocks. However, he and CEO Greg Abel have now made Alphabet one of Berkshire Hathaway's largest investments, beginning in Q3 2025. Buffett is impressed by Alphabet's massive $200 billion capital expenditure on AI data centers, which Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian says have payback periods under two years, translating to roughly 20% annualized returns. With the stock trading at less than 17 times forward earnings, further purchases are expected.

The company is transitioning to consumption-based pricing and positioning AI as a growth driver to reignite expansion.

items.title: KeyCorp Raises 2026 Revenue Outlook: What's Driving It?
items.summary: KeyCorp raised its 2026 revenue guidance to 8% growth from 7-8%, driven by strong loan growth (4-5%), NII expansion (9-11%), and improved fee income guidance (6-7% adjusted). The Clearwater acquisition and robust investment banking activity support the outlook. NIM is expected to reach 3.00-3.05% by year-end. Peer banks PNC and Citizens Financial also project solid 2026 growth.

items.title: Can 3M Continue Its Strong Capital Returns to Shareholders?
items.summary: 3M Company returned $3.8 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in the first half of 2026, with $1.8 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization. The company expects adjusted operating cash flow of $5.8-$6.0 billion and free cash flow conversion above 100% for 2026, while raising its quarterly dividend by 6.8% in February 2026. Despite trading above industry valuation averages, 3M shares gained 3.6% over the past year compared to a 27.8% industry decline.

items.title: Coherent Stock Declines 24% in a Month: Is This a Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: Coherent Corp (COHR) has experienced a 24% monthly decline after a 155% annual surge. Despite premium valuation, the company's AI-focused portfolio, strong datacenter revenue growth (58.6% YoY), expanding margins, and capacity expansion plans support a positive long-term outlook. The stock is rated a Buy, though risks include hyperscaler spending cycles and customer concentration.

items.title: TJX International's Adjusted Margin Hits 7.3%: More Upside Ahead?
items.summary: TJX Companies' International division achieved significant profitability gains in Q2 FY2027, with adjusted segment profit margin rising 210 basis points year-over-year to 7.3%. The division reported net sales of $2.09 billion, up 11% from the prior year, driven by higher customer transactions and 7% comparable sales growth. The margin improvement was supported by favorable merchandise margins and expense leverage, while the company continued expansion efforts in Europe.

items.title: Realty Income Teams Up With KKR: Can Private Capital Drive Growth?
items.summary: Realty Income will retain 51% ownership of a 54-property European net lease venture while KKR invests €528 million for 49%, with KKR's returns capped at 6.3%-6.5% IRR. The deal reflects Realty Income's shift toward private capital funding, with public equity comprising only 18% of first-half 2026 investments versus a historical 47% average. The company raised its 2026 investment guidance to $10 billion, and the venture is expected to close September 30.

items.summary: Digital Realty has announced a strategic joint venture with Ronesans Infrastructure to enter the Turkish market. The partnership will develop a next-generation data center campus in Ankara with over 22MW of carrier-neutral IT capacity, with completion targeted for 2028. Plans also include expansion into Istanbul to create a connected regional infrastructure platform serving cloud, AI, and enterprise digital infrastructure demands.

items.title: CIEN's New Venture Fund: Can it Turn AI Networking Into Growth Engine?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation launched Ciena Ventures, a $200 million corporate venture capital program focused on next-generation connectivity technologies including networking infrastructure, data centers, and optical interconnects. The company expects its addressable market to reach $50 billion by 2029 driven by AI-driven bandwidth demand, with fiscal 2027 revenue projected to grow at least 30% to $8.3-$8.4 billion. However, Ciena faces intense competition from Cisco and Arista Networks in the AI networking space.

items.title: Is This the Right Time to Retain Resmed Stock in Your Portfolio?
items.summary: Resmed is divesting its MatrixCare business for $490 million to streamline its Residential Care Software segment and focus on higher-growth platforms. The company's Masks segment showed strong 13% revenue growth in fiscal 2026, driven by product innovation and improved compliance rates. However, macroeconomic pressures and intense competition pose operational risks.

items.title: Netlist vs. Sandisk: Which AI Memory Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Netlist and Sandisk are both capitalizing on AI-driven demand for advanced memory technologies. Netlist has tripled revenues to $214.7M in H1 2026 with a strategic Samsung alliance, but relies heavily on DRAM resales. Sandisk shows stronger scale with datacenter revenues up 103% sequentially and $93.9B in forward revenue commitments through new business models. Netlist trades at a lower valuation (2.33X forward sales vs. 4.44X for Sandisk) and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) versus Sandisk's Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: Credo vs. Broadcom: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Pick?
items.summary: Credo Technology and Broadcom are both benefiting from the AI infrastructure buildout, but with different strategies. Credo shows stronger growth momentum with 115% revenue growth and 48.2% operating margins, while Broadcom offers massive scale with $16.7B in AI chip revenues and 67.9% operating margins. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, with Credo trading at a slightly lower valuation multiple (9.5X vs 9.93X forward sales).

items.title: Atlassian vs. ServiceNow: Which Cloud Software Stock Has an Edge?
items.summary: Atlassian and ServiceNow are both benefiting from AI adoption in enterprise software, but they face different near-term dynamics. Atlassian shows stronger execution with 31% cloud revenue growth driven by its Rovo AI product and larger customer deals, while trading at a more attractive 5.96X forward sales multiple. ServiceNow's AI ACV exceeded $1 billion with strong adoption, but faces margin pressure from rising AI consumption and hyperscaler reliance. Atlassian receives a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) versus ServiceNow's #4 (Sell), giving TEAM a clearer edge.

items.title: In National Advertising Division Challenge, Zuru Voluntarily Modifies Challenged Incentivized Review Practices
items.summary: Zuru Edge Limited has voluntarily discontinued its incentivized review program and modified practices to comply with FTC Endorsement Guides following a challenge by Procter & Gamble. The company ran a Facebook group for six years offering product reimbursement to reviewers without requiring disclosure of this material connection. Zuru has now discontinued the group and implemented clear disclosure requirements for future incentivized reviews.

items.title: Chewy vs. TJX Companies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Chewy, a digital-first pet retailer with an 8.6B market cap, against TJX Companies, a brick-and-mortar off-price retail powerhouse with a 139B market cap. While Chewy offers a cheaper P/S ratio (0.7x vs 2.3x) and growing Autoship subscription revenue, TJX demonstrates superior profitability with a 9.1% net margin versus Chewy's 1.8%, a lower P/E ratio (23.3x vs 32.65x), and stronger free cash flow ($4.9B vs $562.4M). The author recommends TJX Companies as the better buy, citing its consistent ability to beat expectations, strong customer demand for value, and proven track record of profitability across economic cycles.

items.title: BAC Warns of Q3 Capital Markets Weakness: Will Fee Income Take a Hit?
items.summary: Bank of America expects Q3 investment banking fees of $1.6-$1.8B, down ~15% year-over-year, with trading revenues flat. However, wealth management AUM fees projected to rise 10-15% should offset some weakness. CEO Moynihan noted a 'very strong' deal pipeline, suggesting the slowdown may be timing-related rather than structural.

items.title: 2 Non-AI Giants to Buy on Solid Guidance and Lucrative Valuation
items.summary: Centene Corp. and Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. have both raised their 2026 guidance with significant earnings improvements. Despite year-to-date gains exceeding 50%, both stocks maintain attractive valuations and hold Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings, suggesting further upside potential for the remainder of 2026.

items.title: 3 AI Stocks Poised to Outperform Micron and Sandisk as the Next Infrastructure Bottleneck Builds
items.summary: As AI infrastructure demands evolve beyond chips and memory, three companies are positioned to capitalize on emerging bottlenecks: Innodata provides data organization services with 58% revenue growth; Nebius offers neocloud services with expanding data center capacity and rising per-megawatt contract values; and Vertiv supplies critical liquid cooling solutions for AI infrastructure with 24% revenue growth and accelerating demand.

items.title: The AI Company You Haven't Heard of -- But Should Keep on Your Radar
items.summary: Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell technology company founded in 2001, is positioned to benefit significantly from AI infrastructure expansion. The company helps data centers obtain electricity faster by generating power on-site, addressing grid capacity constraints. After years of losses, Bloom Energy achieved profitability in early 2026 with 166% revenue growth in Q2, driven by major enterprise customers like Oracle. As data center power consumption is projected to reach 12% of U.S. electricity by 2030, Bloom Energy could become a standard supplier in the rapidly expanding data-center ecosystem.

items.title: Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Market Outlook 2026-2035 - Featuring Profiles of Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and Sarepta Therapeutics
items.summary: The global oligonucleotide therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 7.7 billion in 2025 to USD 72.1 billion by 2035, expanding at a 23.4% CAGR. Growth is driven by advances in RNA-based medicine, targeted delivery technologies, expanding applications beyond rare diseases into chronic and metabolic conditions, and increasing regulatory approvals. Antisense oligonucleotides lead the market at 39.9% share, while subcutaneous administration dominates at 56.4%. North America commands 57.9% market share.

items.summary: Cloudflare (NET) is positioned as the stronger investment compared to CrowdStrike (CRWD) due to faster projected growth driven by AI security, SASE, and Zero Trust demand. items.title: Can Audience Unlimited Accelerate Trade Desk's Growth Momentum?
items.summary: The Trade Desk is rolling out Audience Unlimited, an AI-powered platform designed to simplify third-party data selection and activation for advertisers. items.title: Parexel to Lead Sessions at DPHARM 2026 on AI, Talent and the Future of Clinical Operations
items.summary: Parexel announced it will lead three expert panel sessions at DPHARM 2026 in Boston on enterprise AI adoption, workforce readiness, and patient-centric drug development. items.title: Cybersecurity Is the Next Big Market for Artificial Intelligence (AI), According to Jensen Huang. This Super Stock-Split Stock Is the One to Own.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang proposes that cybersecurity will become AI's next major use case, as AI systems can identify and exploit code vulnerabilities at scale. CrowdStrike, positioned as Nvidia's top security partner, is well-positioned to capitalize on this trend with its cloud-native Falcon platform already embedded in corporate networks and expanding across multiple security modules.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Investors with Substantial Losses Have Opportunity to Lead Class Action Lawsuit Before November 2, 2026 Deadline, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP Announces - HIMS
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. alleging the telehealth company made false statements about consumer privacy and billing practices. The FTC filed a lawsuit on July 29, 2026, claiming Hims & Hers shared sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms like Meta and Snap, and charged consumers for prescriptions immediately after intake forms despite promising consultation with medical providers. The stock declined nearly 15% following the FTC announcement. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status before November 2, 2026.

items.title: Jeff Bezos Built Amazon Into a $1.8 Trillion Company. Here's How Andy Jassy Is Making It Worth Even More.
items.summary: Andy Jassy has increased Amazon's market cap by 50% to $2.7 trillion since becoming CEO. AWS, which Jassy previously led, is driving profitability with 60.5% of Amazon's operating profit and 36.8% year-over-year sales growth. Despite massive capital expenditure increases to $220 billion in 2026, Amazon's P/E ratio of 20 is considered attractive compared to its historical average of 50, positioning the stock for long-term growth.

items.title: The 10-Year Treasury Bond Yields Nearly 5% Right Now. Here's Why I'd Still Choose PepsiCo for Passive Income.
items.summary: With 10-year Treasury bonds yielding nearly 5% compared to PepsiCo's 4.3% dividend yield, the author argues PepsiCo remains the better long-term passive income choice due to its 54-year streak of annual dividend increases and potential for capital appreciation, while Treasury bonds offer fixed payments that don't grow with inflation.

items.title: ROSEN, LEADING INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Pentair plc Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - PNR
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Pentair plc, alleging that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding significant inventory destocking in the Pool channel that adversely affected sales and operating income. Investors who purchased Pentair ordinary shares between March 11, 2025 and July 14, 2026 may be entitled to compensation. The deadline to serve as lead plaintiff is October 2, 2026.

items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against EquipmentShare.com Inc (NASDAQ: EQPT) alleging that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding undisclosed related party transactions and failed to disclose material adverse facts about the company's business and financial statements. Investors who purchased EQPT securities during the IPO in January 2026 or between January 23 and June 23, 2026 are encouraged to seek counsel before the September 21, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

items.title: Even With 10-Year Treasury Yields at a 20-Month High, I'd Still Rather Buy This S&P 500 Dividend Stock for Passive Income in September.
items.summary: Despite 10-year Treasury yields reaching a 20-month high of 4.8% compared to PepsiCo's 4.2% dividend yield, the author argues PepsiCo is the better long-term investment. While Treasuries offer stability, their fixed returns cannot keep pace with inflation. PepsiCo, as a Dividend King with 50+ consecutive annual dividend increases, offers growth potential and inflation protection through business expansion and rising dividends that Treasuries cannot match.

A similar notice is issued for Flotek Industries (FTK) investors regarding a separate class action.

items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed securities class actions against Alibaba Group Holding Limited and Flotek Industries, Inc. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities requiring Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to timely file earnings reports. Investors are encouraged to join the class action by the October 27, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

items.title: C3.ai vs. UiPath: What Revenue Trends Between These Artificial Intelligence Companies Tell Investors
items.summary: UiPath demonstrates stronger financial performance with consistent year-over-year revenue growth and a market cap of $7.2B, while C3.ai has experienced significant revenue contraction over eight quarters, declining from $108.7M to $52.4M. C3.ai's challenges were exacerbated by CEO Thomas Siebel's temporary departure in 2025, though his return in June and a 73% quarter-over-quarter increase in customer bookings suggest potential recovery ahead.

items.title: Dell Booked More AI Server Orders in 3 Months Than It Recorded in Total Revenue
items.summary: Dell Technologies received $60.9 billion in AI server orders during Q2 FY2027, exceeding its total quarterly revenue of $47 billion. The company exited with a record $95 billion backlog and raised full-year revenue guidance to $192 billion (69% growth). However, operating cash flow declined to $2.2 billion despite tripled net income, raising concerns about Dell's ability to convert orders into delivered systems and collect cash on schedule.

items.title: $10,000 in Tesla When It Joined the S&P 500 Would Be About $15,700 Today. An Index Fund Would Have Done Better.
items.summary: Tesla stock purchased at $695 when it joined the S&P 500 in December 2020 has returned 57% over nearly six years, translating to roughly 8% annually. However, an S&P 500 index fund investment would have grown the same $10,000 to approximately $20,500 (13% annually), significantly outperforming Tesla. Despite the company tripling its revenue and achieving profitability, most of its growth was already priced into the initial valuation, causing the stock's P/E ratio to compress from 900x to 330x earnings.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Dirt Cheap “Magnificent Seven” Stock Could Be the Biggest Winner of the Trillion-Dollar AI Race – Here’s the Case.
items.summary: The article argues that Alphabet, trading at a cheap 15x forward earnings valuation, could be the biggest winner in the AI race compared to other Magnificent Seven stocks. Unlike chip makers Nvidia and Micron who only profit from selling products, Alphabet benefits from AI as both a provider and user of AI technology, positioning it for success regardless of which chip designer gains market share. The company's Google Search dominance (90%+ market share) generates $81 billion in ad revenue, while its Google Cloud AI business is experiencing explosive growth.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Has Paid Exactly 1 Dividend Since 1965. Here's Where the Cash Goes Instead.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway has maintained its no-dividend policy since 1967, instead reinvesting earnings into acquisitions and share buybacks. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the company continues this strategy, recently acquiring Taylor Morrison for $8.5 billion and increasing its Alphabet stake by $17 billion. Abel has also accelerated share repurchases to $8 billion since April, while maintaining over $350 billion in cash reserves.

items.title: The Cooper Companies (NASDAQ: COO) Scrutinized Over U.S. Channel Inventory Reductions Driving Stock Sharply Lower -- HBSS
items.summary: The Cooper Companies' stock plummeted 14.6% on September 10, 2026, after Q3 2026 earnings revealed significant U.S. channel inventory destocking at its CooperVision segment. The company reduced full-year revenue guidance to flat or down 2% organically, attributing the decline entirely to inventory reductions. Hagens Berman has opened an investigation into whether Cooper was sufficiently transparent about its sales practices and potential securities law violations.

items.title: REGN 2-DAY DEADLINE ALERT: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors Alerted to September 14, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline in Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals over allegations that the company made false and misleading statements regarding a Phase 3 clinical trial of Fianlimab for melanoma treatment. The trial failed to reach statistical significance on its primary endpoint, causing an $11 billion market cap loss. Investors claim Regeneron concealed flawed statistical assumptions and slow event rates while expressing confidence in the trial's success. The lead plaintiff deadline is September 14, 2026.

items.title: Dividend King Altria Recently Raised Its Quarterly Dividend by Nearly 5%. Is the Stock a Buy?
items.summary: Altria Group raised its quarterly dividend by 4.7% to $1.11 per share, maintaining its 57-year streak as a Dividend King with a 6.15% yield. However, the company faces headwinds from declining cigarette volumes and concerning cash flow metrics, with dividends paid exceeding free cash flow in the first half of 2026. While the dividend appears sustainable due to management's commitment to the streak, investors should monitor quarterly results closely for balance sheet deterioration.

items.title: Cerebras Systems vs. IonQ: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two high-performance computing companies: Cerebras Systems, which specializes in AI hardware with wafer-scale chips, and IonQ, which develops quantum computing systems. While Cerebras shows strong 75.7% revenue growth, IonQ demonstrates superior momentum with 202% revenue growth in 2025 and 287% YoY growth in Q2 2026. The author recommends IonQ as the better buy due to its faster scaling, cleaner balance sheet (0.0x debt-to-equity), and positioning in the emerging quantum computing market, despite both companies operating at significant losses.

items.title: Shareholders who lost money in shares of Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) should contact Wolf Haldenstein Immediately
items.summary: Wolf Haldenstein has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) on behalf of investors who purchased shares between November 17, 2025, and August 13, 2026. The complaint alleges that Innventure and its executives overstated the value and likelihood of Accelsius's DarkNX data-center project, leading to inflated revenue and cash flow projections. On August 13, 2026, Innventure suspended its 2026 guidance after disclosing that the DarkNX deployment site was no longer available, causing the stock to plummet 55% from $3.60 to $1.62 per share.

items.title: 3 Agentic AI Stocks to Own Before AI Changes the World as We Know It
items.summary: The article highlights three agentic AI stocks positioned to benefit from the rapid advancement of AI agents: Palantir Technologies with its AI platform for controlling and monitoring AI agents, Salesforce with its Agentforce platform showing 240% ARR growth, and Meta with its new Muse AI agent offering personal AI services across free and paid tiers to generate new revenue streams.

items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) for investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Bloom Energy made false and misleading statements regarding its sourcing of scandium from China through intermediaries, misrepresenting its supply chain dependencies. The deadline to join the class action is September 28, 2026.

items.title: The $760 Billion AI Risk That Nobody Is Talking About. But Should.
items.summary: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta are expected to spend $760 billion on AI infrastructure capex in 2026, an 80% increase from 2025. While AI demand is real and supported by customer commitments, investors should question whether this massive spending will generate attractive returns long-term. The risk lies in potential overcapacity if AI becomes more efficient, computing costs drop, or demand doesn't materialize as expected—similar to previous technology cycles.

items.title: 1 Top Warren Buffett Stock for Dividend Investors
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO Greg Abel has initiated a position in Macy's, purchasing 7.3 million shares valued at $173 million. The department store offers an attractive 3.4% dividend yield, a 29% payout ratio, and trades at a P/E of 9 compared to the S&P 500's 26. With positive same-store sales growth and a turnaround strategy underway, Macy's presents both dividend income and upside potential for investors.

items.summary: GameStop director Alain Attal purchased 5,000 shares for $100,000 on September 10, 2026, expanding his direct holdings to 601,464 shares valued at $12.26 million. Multiple insiders have been buying GameStop shares recently, suggesting confidence in the company's continued momentum.

items.title: Kimberly Clark is Down 20% From Its 52-Week High. Is the Dip Worth Buying?
items.summary: Kimberly Clark, a Dividend King with an attractive 5% yield, has fallen 20% from its 52-week high. However, the company faces significant headwinds including lowered full-year guidance, a major acquisition of Kenvue that will increase leverage, high dividend payout ratio of 85%, and underperformance compared to better-run competitors like Procter & Gamble. Only aggressive dividend investors should consider buying at current levels.

items.title: Arm vs. Credo Technology Group: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Arm Holdings and Credo Technology Group as semiconductor investment options in 2026. Arm provides chip architecture blueprints with a strong royalty-based business model and 93.88% gross margins, while Credo offers high-speed connectivity solutions with explosive 205.7% revenue growth and 35.4% net margins. The author recommends Credo despite its customer concentration risk, citing its impressive triple-digit growth trajectory and essential role in AI data center infrastructure.

items.title: Astera Labs vs. Applied Materials: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two semiconductor-related companies: Astera Labs, a fast-growing AI data center connectivity specialist with 115% revenue growth but heavy customer concentration and high valuation multiples, versus Applied Materials, an established semiconductor equipment manufacturer with $5.7B in free cash flow, slower but stable growth, and more attractive valuation ratios. The author recommends Applied Materials for long-term investors due to its lower valuation, broader market position, and consistent cash generation despite Astera's impressive growth trajectory.

items.title: Adobe vs. Ciena: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Adobe and Ciena as investment options for 2026. Adobe offers proven profitability with a 30% net margin and strong free cash flow of $9.9 billion, trading at attractive valuations (P/E 14.23). Ciena shows explosive growth with 18.8% revenue increase and record backlogs driven by AI data center demand, though at a premium valuation (P/E 74.66). The author recommends Ciena for long-term investors due to accelerating business momentum and extraordinary demand visibility, despite acknowledging customer concentration risks.

items.title: CIEN Falls 15.2% in a Week as AI Growth Faces Persistent Supply Risks
items.summary: Ciena Corporation shares dropped 15.2% despite beating Q3 earnings expectations and strong AI-driven cloud-provider revenue growth of 82%. While backlog reached $8.5B with expectations to exceed $10B by year-end, persistent supply constraints through 2027-2028, high customer concentration (41.7% from two providers), and elevated valuation at 35.7X forward P/E create execution risks that offset positive fundamentals.

items.title: Ciena's 2027 Growth Guide Raises the Stakes for AI Optical Demand
items.summary: Ciena reported strong Q3 results with 37% revenue growth to $1.67B and 215% adjusted EPS growth to $2.11, driven by AI-related networking demand from hyperscalers. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenues of $8.3B-$8.4B with an $8.5B backlog expected to exceed $10B by year-end. However, supply constraints are expected to persist through 2028, potentially limiting growth conversion.

items.title: ALH vs. WSM: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: In a comparison of two Retail - Home Furnishings stocks, Alliance Laundry Holdings (ALH) emerges as the superior value option over Williams-Sonoma (WSM). ALH holds a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with stronger earnings outlook improvements, a lower forward P/E ratio of 15.78 versus WSM's 23.54, and a better Value grade of B compared to WSM's D. ALH's PEG ratio of 0.92 and P/B ratio of 8.35 also indicate better valuation metrics than WSM's 2.40 and 12.31 respectively.

items.title: BigBear.ai Stock Dives 29% in the Past 3 Months: Hold or Fold?
items.summary: BigBear.ai (BBAI) has declined 29.4% over three months despite reporting 13% Q2 revenue growth to $36.7M and a strong $409.8M cash position. The company faces headwinds from modest growth relative to AI opportunity, persistent losses with adjusted EBITDA deteriorating to -$11.6M, heavy dependence on government contract conversion, and intense competition from larger players like Palantir. While the company benefits from rising AI demand and has strategic M&A plans, investors remain cautious about profitability and execution risks.

items.title: ADBE Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Subscription Growth
items.summary: Adobe reported Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings of $6.13 per share and revenues of $6.76 billion, both beating consensus estimates. Subscription revenues grew 13.7% to $6.58 billion, while AI-first ARR exceeded $650 million with over 150% year-over-year growth. The company raised its fiscal 2026 revenue and earnings guidance despite margin compression from increased operating expenses.

items.title: Cisco (CSCO) Down 5.3% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: Cisco Systems reported strong Q4 fiscal 2026 results with earnings of $1.22 per share (up 23% YoY) and revenues of $17.252 billion (up 18% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. Networking revenues surged 28% YoY driven by AI infrastructure and data center growth. The company provided strong fiscal 2027 guidance projecting revenues of $72.2-$73.4 billion and hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenues of $7.5 billion. Despite gross margin pressure from hardware mix and memory costs, operating leverage expanded margins. However, shares have underperformed the S&P 500 by 5.3% since the earnings report.

items.title: Coherent (COHR) Down 10.4% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: Coherent reported strong Q4 earnings with adjusted EPS beating estimates by 7.4% and revenues up 33.8% year-over-year, driven primarily by datacenter and communications segment growth. Despite solid fundamentals and upward estimate revisions, the stock has declined 10.4% since earnings. The company projects continued growth with Q1 FY2027 guidance implying 45.6% year-over-year revenue growth, though concerns exist around high inventory levels and substantial capital expenditure requirements.

items.title: Illinois Tool Exhibits Strong Prospects Despite Persisting Headwinds
items.summary: Illinois Tool Works (ITW) demonstrates broad-based growth across welding, electronics, and construction segments with 3-4% expected organic revenue growth in 2026. Enterprise initiatives added 120 basis points to operating margin. However, the company faces headwinds from weak automotive production and soft foodservice demand, with cost pressures impacting margins.

items.title: Adobe Q3 Earnings Call Centers on Agentic AI and Freemium
items.summary: Adobe reported Q3 FY2026 earnings beating estimates with $6.76B in revenue and $6.13 EPS. The company is prioritizing agentic AI as its next platform shift and emphasizing user acquisition through freemium models over immediate pricing increases. AI-first ARR exceeded $650M with 150%+ YoY growth. Leadership transition announced with Anil Chakravarthy becoming CEO on Dec. 1. Full-year guidance raised while maintaining 10.2% ARR growth target.

items.title: Can Ciena Sustain Its Strong Growth Amid Rising Optical Demand?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation reported record fiscal Q3 revenue of $1.67B (up 37% YoY) with adjusted EPS surging 215% to $2.11, driven by strong optical networks demand from AI infrastructure investments. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3-8.4B, though supply constraints remain a limiting factor. Competitors Corning and Viavi Solutions also benefit from AI infrastructure and optical connectivity tailwinds.

items.title: FPS Set to Report Q4 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: Forgent Power Solutions is expected to report Q4 fiscal 2026 revenues of $425.6 million with EPS of 23 cents on Sept. 15. The company benefits from strong data center and grid infrastructure spending, with Powertrain Solutions revenues surging 248% in Q3. However, backlog near $2 billion and strong bookings (up 308% YoY) support future growth, though new facility ramp-up costs may limit margin expansion. The Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat given 0.00% Earnings ESP and Rank #3 rating.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 82% of Berkshire's $360 Billion Portfolio Concentrated in 10 Superstar Stocks
items.summary: Greg Abel has taken over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway following Warren Buffett's retirement. Abel maintains Buffett's strategy of portfolio concentration, with 82% ($294 billion) of Berkshire's $360 billion invested assets concentrated in 10 stocks. A key difference is Abel's willingness to invest in tech stocks like Apple and Alphabet, while maintaining Buffett's core holdings in financial stocks and 'indefinite' holdings like Coca-Cola and American Express.

Cerebras is recommended as the better investment due to consistent high growth (74% YoY in Q2 2026) and strong profitability (47% net margin), while BigBear.ai faces revenue inconsistency, customer concentration risks, and ongoing legal challenges despite showing some growth catalysts from increased defense spending.

The foundry industry generated record revenues in 2025, with TSMC controlling approximately 72% of global foundry revenue, and capacity constraints are expected to drive wafer price increases.

items.title: Bloom Energy vs. FuelCell Energy: Which Data Center Fuel Cell Maker Is the Better Buy Right Now?
items.summary: Bloom Energy and FuelCell Energy are competing to power AI data centers. Bloom Energy has emerged as the market leader with $1.065B in Q2 2026 revenue (up 166% YoY), a $20B backlog, and a 225% year-to-date stock surge, but trades at a premium valuation. FuelCell Energy is a riskier, earlier-stage play with a $3.6B backlog and recent $300M capital raise, but faces execution challenges and currently operates at a loss.

items.title: Adobe Systems (ADBE) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates
items.summary: Adobe reported Q3 2026 earnings of $6.13 per share, beating consensus estimates of $6.08, with revenues of $6.76 billion exceeding expectations. However, the company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revision trends. Adobe shares have underperformed the S&P 500 by 38.8 percentage points year-to-date. The stock's near-term outlook remains uncertain pending management commentary.

items.title: ROSEN, THE FIRST FILING FIRM, Encourages Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm – BABA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is seeking lead plaintiffs for a securities class action lawsuit against Alibaba Group Holding Limited (BABA) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Alibaba made false and misleading statements regarding its control by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), which would classify it as a Chinese military company under the National Defense Authorization Act, and failed to disclose ongoing distillation attacks against third-party AI models. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 5, 2026.

items.title: ROSEN, NATIONAL TRIAL LAWYERS, Encourages Innventure, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - INV
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased Innventure, Inc. securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 of an important October 27, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in an ongoing securities class action. The lawsuit alleges that Innventure made materially false statements regarding Accelsius Holdings LLC's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly had no credible basis, resulting in overstated revenue and cash flow targets for 2026.

items.title: An Nvidia Move Just Put AMD and Intel on the Defensive
items.summary: Nvidia is entering the server CPU market with its Vera chip based on Arm architecture, threatening Intel and AMD's traditional dominance in x86 processors. With expected $20 billion in Vera CPU revenue this year and projections to double next year, Nvidia is capitalizing on the shift toward agentic AI and inference workloads. Nvidia's lower valuation (P/E of 29) compared to AMD (122) and Intel (88) positions it as a stronger investment opportunity.

items.title: Can Hypersonic Weapons Production Boost Leidos' Growth Prospects?
items.summary: Leidos Holdings is advancing its role in U.S. hypersonic weapons programs, including the Thermal Protection Shield (TPS) and Common Hypersonic Glide Body (CHGB) programs, as these capabilities transition from development to production. The company's expertise in guidance systems, sensors, and precision munitions positions it to benefit from rising U.S. investment in hypersonic technologies and growing geopolitical demand for advanced defense systems.

The complaint claims the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked credible evidence of execution. Investors who purchased shares between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are eligible to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: EYE or CL: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two Consumer Products - Staples stocks reveals that National Vision (EYE) offers better value than Colgate-Palmolive (CL). EYE has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a lower forward P/E of 17.51, and a Value grade of B. CL has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold), higher forward P/E of 22.74, and a Value grade of D, making EYE the superior value option.

items.title: Franco-Nevada (FNV) Up 12.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Franco-Nevada shares have gained 12.5% since its Q2 2026 earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. While revenues surged 57% year-over-year to $581 million and adjusted earnings rose 46%, the company missed consensus EPS estimates ($1.81 vs. $1.95 expected). Profitability margins contracted despite strong revenue growth. The company maintains a debt-free balance sheet with $1.01 billion in cash and expects to track toward the upper half of its 2026 GEO sales guidance of 510,000-570,000 ounces.

items.title: Cardinal (CAH) Up 2.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Cardinal Health reported Q4 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.91, beating consensus by 20.3%, with full-year adjusted EPS up 37% year-over-year. While revenues missed estimates, the company raised fiscal 2027 guidance to $12.40-$12.60 EPS, implying 13-15% growth. Shares have outperformed the S&P 500 over the past month, though the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Can Ciena Convert Its $8.5B Backlog Despite Supply Constraints?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation reported a $8.5B backlog in Q3 fiscal 2026, up $800M sequentially, with expectations to exceed $10B by year-end. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenues of at least $8.3-$8.4B (30% YoY growth) and is investing in supply chain security through 2029 agreements. Competitors Nokia and Cisco also show strong AI/cloud order momentum, though supply constraints remain the limiting factor for revenue conversion across the optical networking sector.

items.title: COO Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, Revenues Miss on Destocking, Stock Down
items.summary: Cooper Companies reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.15, beating estimates by 3.6%, but revenues of $1.066 billion missed expectations by 3.0%. CooperVision faced pressure from U.S. channel inventory reductions, while CooperSurgical showed resilience with 2% revenue growth. The stock fell 15.9% after-hours as management expects continued destocking headwinds in Q4, though underlying U.S. consumption remains healthy.

items.title: Compared to Estimates, C3.ai (AI) Q1 Earnings: A Look at Key Metrics
items.summary: C3.ai reported Q1 revenue of $52.38 million, down 25.5% year-over-year but beating consensus estimates by 1.79%. The company posted an EPS of -$0.20, a significant improvement from -$0.37 a year ago and beating estimates by 23.08%. While subscription revenue declined 18.5% YoY, gross margins improved in both professional services and subscription segments. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Lowe's Just Hit a 52-Week Low. Is It an Obvious Buy or Should Investors Pause?
items.summary: Lowe's stock has fallen 25% over the past year to a 52-week low of $199, driven by management's trimmed guidance citing macroeconomic pressures including high mortgage rates, inflation, and tariffs that have slowed DIY projects. While the company's fundamentals remain solid with growing Pro and digital segments, the stock presents a mixed opportunity: attractive for long-term dividend investors seeking a 2.45% yield, but lacking near-term catalysts for growth-oriented investors.

items.title: Proofpoint Expands AI-Powered Investigations to Microsoft 365 and Deepens Insider Risk Visibility into AI Activity
items.summary: Proofpoint announced enhancements to its Prism Investigator and Human Communications Intelligence capabilities, enabling direct connections to Microsoft 365 for AI-driven investigations and incorporating AI interactions into insider threat investigations. The updates aim to help organizations investigate insider risk faster by understanding intent across both human and AI communications.

items.title: AI Labs Integrates Google’s Gemini into AIV Chatbot to Launch Next-Generation Investment Analytics Platform
items.summary: Singapore-based AI Labs has integrated Google's Gemini AI into its AIV Chatbot, creating an advanced investment analytics platform for analyzing cryptocurrencies and technology stocks. The platform organizes investment research around market outlook, technical analysis, fundamentals and risk, presenting structured analysis rather than simple buy/sell signals. Gemini's multimodal capabilities enable the chatbot to analyze earnings releases, market data, charts and financial documents, with potential to evolve into an interactive investment research assistant accessible to retail investors.

items.title: $HAREHOLDER ALERT: The M&A Class Action Firm Continues to Investigate the Merger – AUUD, TECH, CZR and CBAN
items.summary: Monteverde & Associates PC is investigating four major merger and acquisition deals to determine if they are fair to shareholders: Auddia's merger with McCarthy Finney (1:1 stock exchange), Bio-Techne's sale to Merck KGaA ($73/share), Caesars Entertainment's sale to Fertitta Gaming ($31/share plus ticking consideration), and Colony Bankcorp's merger with First Reliance Bancshares ($19.75 cash or 0.94 stock exchange).

items.title: Deadline Alert: Alibaba Group Holding Limited (BABA) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP About Securities Fraud Lawsuit
items.summary: Alibaba Group Holding Limited faces a class action securities fraud lawsuit covering the period from June 26, 2025 to June 24, 2026. The lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose its control by or affiliation with China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), which classified it as a Chinese military company under the National Defense Authorization Act. Additionally, Anthropic accused Alibaba of illicitly accessing its Claude AI model through fraudulent accounts. These revelations caused Alibaba's stock to drop approximately 3.9% on June 10, 2026, and an additional 2.7% on June 24, 2026. The deadline to file a lead plaintiff motion is October 5, 2026.

items.title: Oracle & Adobe Earnings Ahead: Which Software Giant Has More AI Upside?
items.summary: Oracle and Adobe are set to report earnings on September 10, 2026, with both companies positioned as AI investment plays. Oracle is experiencing explosive cloud infrastructure growth with 58-64% expected cloud revenue surge and a massive $638 billion backlog, justifying its premium 25X forward earnings valuation. Adobe faces AI disruption concerns but trades at a 50% discount to Oracle at 13X forward earnings, with AI-first ARR tripled YoY to $500 million. Zacks rates Oracle as a Buy (#2) and Adobe as a Sell (#4), suggesting Oracle's stronger growth trajectory makes it more compelling despite Adobe's attractive valuation.

items.title: Is Iren Stock a Buy Now?
items.summary: Iren is pivoting from Bitcoin mining to AI cloud services, with AI revenue surging from $16.4M to $128.8M year-over-year. The company secured a $9.7B Microsoft deal and has contracts with multiple AI firms. While facing massive capital expenditures ($25-30B projected for 2027) and recent losses, the stock is positioned for growth-focused investors betting on AI compute demand.

items.title: Digital Provenance Platform Market to Reach $18.24 Billion by 2035 as AI-Generated Content Drives Demand for Digital Authentication | Research by SNS Insider
items.summary: The global Digital Provenance Platform Market is projected to grow from $2.72 billion in 2025 to $18.24 billion by 2035, driven by increasing AI-generated content, deepfake concerns, and demand for digital authentication. Software solutions dominate with 73% market share, while cloud deployment leads at 58.5%. North America holds the largest regional share at 45.8%, with the U.S. market expected to reach $15.50 billion by 2035. Key players include Adobe, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and IBM.

items.title: Prediction: This Is What a $10,000 Investment in Amazon Will Be Worth by 2030
items.summary: Amazon stock could potentially reach $600 per share by 2030, turning a $10,000 investment into over $23,000. The growth will be driven primarily by AWS, which is experiencing 37% year-over-year revenue growth and generating 60% of Amazon's operating income despite representing only 21% of revenue. AWS's expansion into AI and cloud computing infrastructure is expected to significantly increase Amazon's overall profit margins.

items.title: Dell vs. HPE: Which Top AI Server Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packard Enterprise both delivered record quarterly results driven by explosive AI-server demand. Dell posted 58% revenue growth with AI-optimized server revenue doubling, while HPE achieved 34% revenue growth with strong server and networking gains. Both companies raised full-year guidance significantly. Dell gets a slight edge as the better buy due to its larger AI-server position and stronger growth, though HPE offers better valuation metrics for value-oriented investors.

items.title: My Top Dividend Growth Stock to Buy in September and Hold Forever
items.summary: PepsiCo is recommended as a top dividend growth stock to buy in September. The company is a Dividend King with 54 years of consecutive dividend increases, currently offering a 4.3% yield. Despite underperforming the S&P 500 and trading down 14.3% over six months, PepsiCo's valuation is attractive relative to peers, making it an appealing opportunity for long-term dividend investors seeking stable income.

items.title: GE HealthCare Moves StarGuide GX 4D SPECT/CT Toward FDA Clearance
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies has submitted its next-generation StarGuide GX digital SPECT/CT system for FDA 510(k) clearance following CE Mark approval in Europe. The system features dual-sided CZT detectors, NVIDIA RTX computing, and rapid collimator exchange, designed to support emerging radioligand therapies including alpha emitters like Actinium-225 and Lead-212. Despite the regulatory milestone, GEHC stock declined 3% following the announcement.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo study. The complaint claims the study's preliminary statistical assumptions were flawed, the treatment arm showed no meaningful clinical differentiation from standard therapies, and the study was unlikely to achieve statistical significance on its primary endpoint. The class period covers securities purchased between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026.

items.title: NVST or ABT: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two Medical Products stocks, Envista (NVST) emerges as the superior value option over Abbott (ABT). NVST holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a Value grade of B, featuring a lower forward P/E ratio of 17.51 and PEG ratio of 1.28. ABT has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Value grade of C, with higher valuations at P/E of 19.11 and PEG of 1.96. Based on stronger earnings outlook and more attractive valuation metrics, NVST is positioned as the better value investment.

items.title: Simon Property (SPG) Down 3.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: Simon Property Group reported strong Q2 2026 earnings with FFO of $3.29 per share beating estimates by 3.46% and raising full-year guidance. Despite solid operational metrics including 96% occupancy and 13.9% growth in retailer sales per square foot, the stock has declined 3.5% since the earnings report and underperformed the S&P 500. The company maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with poor growth and momentum scores.

items.title: ETFs in Spotlight as Bloom Energy is Set to Join the S&P 500 Index
items.summary: Bloom Energy (BE) has been added to the S&P 500 index effective September 21, 2026, following record Q2 revenues of $1.07 billion (up 166% YoY). The company benefits from surging AI data center power demands. While direct stock ownership carries valuation risks (P/E of 67.99), several ETFs offer diversified exposure to Bloom Energy and the clean energy sector.

items.title: Medtronic Is on the Cusp of Becoming a Dividend King. Is the Stock a Buy for Income Investors?
items.summary: Medtronic is one year away from achieving Dividend King status with 49 consecutive years of dividend increases. While the company has a healthy 45% payout ratio and appears well-positioned to reach this milestone, its appeal to income investors may be limited due to slow dividend growth rates. The company is balancing dividend increases with investments in growth drivers like robotic surgery and cardiac products, plus the planned divestiture of its MiniMed diabetes business. For investors seeking both income and capital appreciation, Medtronic could be a solid long-term hold if anticipated earnings growth materializes.

items.title: Amazon Plans to Spend More Than $200 Billion on AI. Is That a Smart Move?
items.summary: Amazon plans to spend $220 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, with a significant portion directed toward AI infrastructure. While this represents a massive bet on AI's future, AWS's strong 37% revenue growth and 63% operating income increase suggest customer demand justifies the investment. However, risks remain around return on investment and potential industry overcapacity, as major tech companies collectively spend $760 billion on AI capex in 2026.

items.title: Medtronic Raises 2027 Outlook as Broad-Based Growth Gains Momentum
items.summary: Medtronic (MDT) raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth guidance to 7.25%-7.75% following a strong first quarter with adjusted EPS of $1.45 (up 15.1% YoY) and revenues of $9.76 billion (up 13.7%). The company's recent acquisitions in neurovascular and pain markets add exposure to faster-growing segments. However, margin expansion remains challenged by unfavorable product mix and tariff pressures, with management targeting only 50 basis points of improvement.

items.title: The Cooper Companies Gears Up to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in Store?
items.summary: The Cooper Companies (COO) is scheduled to report fiscal Q3 2026 results on September 9, with consensus estimates suggesting modest 3.6% sales growth and 0.9% EPS growth. While CooperVision's premium lens portfolio and myopia control products are expected to drive growth, Asia Pacific headwinds and margin pressures from FX and tariffs present challenges. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with no conclusive earnings beat predicted.

items.title: If You Own Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks, Get Ready for a Big Change
items.summary: AI investors should pay attention to significant shifts in the sector driven by new AI models from Meta and Google, recent earnings reports from Broadcom and Snowflake, and comments from Sam Altman regarding data center water consumption. Broadcom's AI chip revenue surged 221% with more growth expected.

items.title: Wall Street Isn't Talking About High-Yield Medtronic Stock -- Here's Why It Should Be
items.summary: Medtronic has undergone strategic restructuring by exiting less profitable businesses and investing in new technologies like its Hugo surgical robot. The company reported its highest annual revenue growth in a decade in fiscal 2026, with Q1 FY2027 revenues jumping 13.7% and management raising full-year guidance. With a 3.08% dividend yield and 48-year dividend increase streak, the stock has risen 15% in three months but remains 30% below its 2021 high, suggesting potential upside for dividend investors.

items.title: This AI Chipmaker Looks Like a Bargain With AI Revenue Set to Double Again Next Year
items.summary: Broadcom, a leading ASIC chip designer, expects its AI semiconductor revenue to double in fiscal 2027 and double again in fiscal 2028. Despite impressive business fundamentals with 48% overall revenue growth and 88% net income growth in Q2 2026, the stock has underperformed the S&P 500, trading at a low 19x forward P/E ratio that doesn't reflect its strong growth prospects.

items.title: Warren Buffett and His Successor, Greg Abel, Have Piled More Than $82 Billion Into This Perennial Winner (No, Not Alphabet!)
items.summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, has resumed aggressive share buybacks after a 21-month hiatus, repurchasing $4.53 billion of Berkshire stock in Q2 2026. Since mid-July 2018, Berkshire has spent over $82 billion retiring nearly 13% of outstanding shares, rewarding long-term investors and boosting earnings per share.

items.summary: Broadcom and Marvell are leading players in the custom AI chip market, with Broadcom expected to control 60% market share by 2027 versus Marvell's 20-25%. items.title: Flex's $4.4B EPC Power Buyout: A Bigger Bet on AI Data Center Growth?
items.summary: Flex Ltd. is acquiring EPC Power for $4.4 billion to expand its AI infrastructure power capabilities, particularly in 800V data center power architectures. items.title: ExxonMobil Has Raised Its Dividend 43 Years Running. Here's the One Year the Streak Almost Broke.
items.summary: ExxonMobil has maintained a 43-year dividend increase streak, but nearly broke it in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic when oil prices turned negative. Unlike competitors BP and Shell that cut dividends, ExxonMobil's CEO pledged to keep the dividend 'sacrosanct,' successfully preserving the streak through modest, steady annual increases.

items.title: Bloom Energy Outpaces Its Industry in a Month: Time to Buy the Stock?
items.summary: Bloom Energy (BE) gained 20% in the past month, outperforming its industry and the S&P 500, driven by rising AI data-center demand and a $5B-to-$25B expansion of its Brookfield partnership for AI power infrastructure. items.title: Salesforce Stock Gains 34% in a Month: Time to Hold or Book Profits?
items.summary: Salesforce shares surged 34% in one month following strong Q2 FY2027 results showing stabilized double-digit revenue growth of 10.8% YoY and accelerating cRPO growth of 14%. Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion with 240% YoY growth, positioning the company as an AI and enterprise data platform beyond traditional CRM. Despite the sharp rally, the stock trades at a reasonable 16.30x forward P/E, below sector averages and major competitors, suggesting room for upside. However, risks include potential pressure on per-user subscription models from AI agents and slower enterprise IT spending amid economic uncertainty.

items.title: Billionaire David Tepper Just Bought These 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That Wall Street Thinks Could Soar by 50% or More

items.title: Walmart Has Gone Practically Nowhere, While Target Is Up 68%. But Only 1 of These Dividend Kings Is a Buy in September.
items.summary: Target has surged 68% year-to-date while Walmart declined 4%, but the article argues Target is the better buy in September. Despite Target's recent momentum under new CEO Michael Fiddleke and positive comparable sales growth, Walmart remains a recession-resilient juggernaut with superior long-term performance. Target trades at a lower P/E ratio (17x vs 39x) and offers a higher dividend yield (2.8% vs 0.9%), while Walmart has demonstrated more consistent revenue growth and operational excellence over decades.

items.title: Nvidia, Palantir, and Meta Platforms Are Rattling Wall Street With This $18.6 Billion Warning

While insider selling can be attributed to tax obligations, the lack of insider buying raises concerns about potential AI bubble risks, as historical patterns show investors often overestimate adoption rates of breakthrough technologies.

items.summary: NetApp shares gained 14.8% over three months driven by record all-flash revenue growth of 46.6%, approximately 350 new AI and data lake modernization deals, and a strong Q1 earnings beat. The company raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $7.975-$8.225 billion and earnings to $9.73-$10.03 per share. However, margin pressures from component costs and demand timing risks remain concerns.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked credible evidence of execution. Investors who purchased shares between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are eligible to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: Strength in Transportation & Electronics Unit Drives 3M: A Sign of More Upside?
items.summary: 3M's Transportation & Electronics segment showed strong growth with revenues up 6.2% to $2.07 billion in Q2 2026, driven by double-digit growth in semiconductor, data center, and aerospace markets. The company raised its 2026 outlook, expecting adjusted organic sales growth above 3.5% and adjusted EPS of $8.80-$8.95, though softness in auto and consumer electronics remains a concern.

items.title: What's Powering Bank of America's Strong Capital Return Strategy?
items.summary: Bank of America demonstrates strong capacity for shareholder returns through robust earnings generation, healthy CET1 capital ratios, and disciplined balance-sheet management. The bank raised its quarterly dividend 14.3% to 32 cents per share and maintains $17 billion in remaining buyback authorization. Strong Q2 2026 results with $9.1 billion net income and 15% revenue growth support continued capital distributions, though a higher G-SIB surcharge from January 2027 may modestly increase capital requirements.

items.title: Workday's Q2 Beat and AI Gains Raise the Stakes for Fiscal 2028 Growth
items.summary: Workday exceeded Q2 expectations with 12.8% revenue growth and 13.9% subscription revenue growth. AI products generated over $100M in new annual contract value with agentic AI ARR approaching $600M (up 200% YoY). The company raised fiscal 2027 margin guidance to 31% and targets 11% subscription growth in fiscal 2028 with at least 2 percentage points of margin expansion. Key challenge remains converting AI adoption into sustainable incremental revenues as core subscription growth moderates.

items.title: Can Local Javelin Production Strengthen Lockheed Martin in India?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin and RTX Corporation's Javelin Joint Venture have signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Advanced Systems to explore co-production of Javelin missiles in India. The initiative aims to establish final assembly and integration facilities in India while maintaining component production in the U.S., strengthening supply-chain resilience and supporting India's defense modernization goals.

items.title: Salesforce's Massive AI Agent Labor Market Could Drive New Upside
items.summary: Salesforce is positioning its Agentforce product as billable digital labor rather than just another AI feature. The company aims to tie consumption revenue directly to corporate labor spending, potentially opening a larger growth market. Success depends on consumption revenue growing faster than software seat losses and maintaining controlled inference costs.

items.title: Nebius Stock Up 254% in a Year: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell?
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) has surged 253.5% over the past year, driven by 454% revenue growth and four AI cloud deals exceeding $1 billion each. The company raised its year-end contracted power target to 5 gigawatts and expects $20-25 billion in capital spending for 2026. However, elevated capital requirements, capacity deployment timelines, and the stock's strong rally suggest caution at current valuation levels. Zacks rates NBIS as a Hold, recommending existing investors hold while new investors await a better entry point.

items.title: AI in Pharmaceutical Market to Hit USD 48.43 Billion by 2035, Growing at 31.76% CAGR – SNS Insider
items.summary: The global AI in pharmaceutical market is projected to grow from USD 3.07 billion in 2025 to USD 48.43 billion by 2035, with a CAGR of 31.76%. The U.S. market is expected to reach USD 15.10 billion and Europe USD 12.60 billion by 2035. Growth is driven by generative AI, adaptive trials reducing patient enrollment by 40%, regulatory endorsement including FDA's qualification of AIM-NASH, and increased venture capital investment in AI-first drug discovery platforms.

items.title: PepsiCo Loses to 30-year U.S. Treasury Bonds on Yield. Here's Why It Wins on Everything Else.
items.summary: While 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds offer a higher yield of 5.25% compared to PepsiCo's 4.1% dividend yield, PepsiCo presents a more attractive long-term investment option. The company has demonstrated 390% stock appreciation over 30 years (920% including dividends), maintains a 54-year streak of dividend increases making it a Dividend King, and generates $9.7 billion in free cash flow—well above its $7.8 billion dividend payout. These factors suggest PepsiCo offers better long-term returns despite lower current income.

However, the company's core business model relies on recurring revenue from parts and services (75% of revenue), which provides stable annuity-like income streams. With valuation metrics below five-year averages and continued AI opportunities, the stock may represent a buying opportunity for aggressive growth investors despite its historical volatility.

items.title: Here's How Many Shares of Procter & Gamble You'd Need for $15,000 in Yearly Dividends

While the stock has underperformed the S&P 500 with only 67% gains over the past decade, it remains an attractive choice for income investors due to its 70-year streak of dividend increases and 136-year history of continuous dividend payments, making it a Dividend King with strong competitive positioning.

items.title: Most Investors Overpay for AI Hype. Nvidia Is the Exception.
items.summary: Nvidia's AI business is delivering exceptional results with Q2 FY2027 revenue doubling to $96.2B and strong free cash flow of $69.9B. The company's upcoming Vera Rubin platform and expanding revenue per data center offer significant growth potential, but risks include massive future spending commitments ($366B), margin pressure, and dependence on customers achieving adequate returns from their AI infrastructure investments.

items.title: Here's How Many Shares of Apple (AAPL) Stock You'd Need for $12,000 in Yearly Dividends
items.summary: To generate $12,000 in annual dividend income from Apple stock, an investor would need to purchase approximately 11,111 shares at a cost of $3.6 million, given Apple's current quarterly dividend of $0.27 per share ($1.08 annually) and stock price around $325. The article cautions that Apple's dividend yield is low at 0.33% and suggests investors may be better served by focusing on Apple's price appreciation potential or seeking dividend income through dividend-focused ETFs instead.

items.title: Broadcom (AVGO) Stock Is Down After Q3 Earnings: Is It Too Soon to Buy the Dip?
items.summary: Broadcom delivered exceptional Q3 results with 85% revenue growth and AI semiconductor revenue skyrocketing 221% to $16.7 billion. Despite beating expectations, AVGO stock fell nearly 3% due to Q4 guidance slightly missing some Wall Street forecasts. The stock is down 15% over the past month and trades at 34X forward earnings, making it more attractive but still vulnerable to high market expectations.

items.summary: A securities class action has been filed against EquipmentShare.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: EQPT) for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding undisclosed related-party transactions with entities owned or controlled by co-founders. Investors who purchased securities between January 23 and June 23, 2026 may be eligible to participate in the class action.

items.title: Jensen Huang Said This Word Exactly 1 Time During Nvidia's Earnings Call, and That Was Enough to Put Artificial Intelligence (AI) Bubble Fears to Rest
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's single use of the word 'visibility' during earnings signals the company's unprecedented insight into AI infrastructure demand across land, power, and supply chains. With top hyperscalers expected to spend $800 billion on capex in 2026 and $1.3 trillion in 2027, Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance and strategic equity stakes in networking and optical companies position it as the architect of AI factories rather than just a chip vendor, suggesting secular demand rather than a bubble.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Retain Cencora Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Cencora's U.S. Healthcare Solutions business demonstrated accelerating momentum with 5% revenue growth and 16% operating income growth in Q3, driven by specialty strength and OneOncology's performance. However, the company faces headwinds from manufacturer list-price reductions, the pending MWI divestiture expected to create a $150 million earnings impact, and regulatory uncertainty around 340B and ASP rules. GLP-1 growth and international operations provide diversification opportunities.

The lawsuit alleges that Hims made materially false and misleading statements regarding consumer health data sharing with third-party advertisers, premature prescription charges despite promised consultations, and undisclosed regulatory scrutiny and potential penalties. items.title: Don't Overlook These 2 AI-Driven Tech Stocks After Earnings: CIEN, NTAP
items.summary: Ciena and NetApp delivered impressive earnings results and raised guidance, capitalizing on AI infrastructure demand. Ciena's optical networking equipment saw 82% YoY cloud provider revenue growth with a raised FY2026 guidance to $6.42B (35% growth). NetApp posted record results with 30% YoY revenue growth to $2.02B and significantly raised FY2027 guidance to $7.98-$8.23B. Both stocks hold Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) ratings.

items.title: Physical AI Infrastructure Market to Reach $327.21 Billion by 2035 as Robotics and Autonomous Systems Accelerate Global Demand | Research by SNS Insider
items.summary: The global Physical AI Infrastructure Market is projected to grow from $14.20 billion in 2025 to $327.21 billion by 2035, with a CAGR of 36.91%. Growth is driven by deployment of AI systems in robotics, autonomous vehicles, smart factories, and edge computing. North America leads with 37% market share, while Asia-Pacific shows the fastest growth at 38.56% CAGR. Compute infrastructure and cloud deployment models dominate, with industrial automation and humanoid robotics as key applications.

items.title: Realty Income's Industrial Expansion: Can it Lift Long-Term Returns?
items.summary: Realty Income (O) is significantly expanding its industrial real estate portfolio, allocating about 75% of Q2 U.S. investments to warehouses and logistics. Industrial assets now represent 65% of global investments with stronger rent escalators (2-3.5% annually) and a 105.8% rent recapture rate. items.title: Fewer Than 30 Companies in the S&P 500 Have Raised Their Dividend for 50 Straight Years. This Financial Stock Is One of Them.
items.summary: S&P Global is highlighted as one of fewer than 30 S&P 500 companies that have raised dividends for 50+ consecutive years, achieving 54 years of increases. The company has delivered over 15% annualized returns over three decades, outperforming the S&P 500's 10.4%. Despite earlier concerns about AI disruption and disappointing Q4 results, S&P Global's dominant 50% market share in credit ratings, asset-light business model with 54% operating margins, and recent earnings guidance raise make it an attractive buy at current valuations of 26.4x earnings.

items.title: Securities Fraud Investigation Into Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) Continues – Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz

Further declines of up to 7% occurred on July 23 after Alphabet announced a significant increase in capital expenditures to $195-205 billion for 2026, negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, and expected margin pressure from reliance on third-party capacity.

items.title: AMP vs. PS: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two Financial - Investment Management stocks, Ameriprise Financial Services (AMP) emerges as the superior value option for investors. AMP holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with an improving earnings outlook and a Value grade of A, supported by a forward P/E of 12.21 and PEG ratio of 1.01. items.title: Steris (STE) Down 2.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: STERIS reported strong Q1 fiscal 2027 results with adjusted EPS of $2.59 (up 10.7% YoY) beating estimates by 1.97%, driven by higher volume, pricing, and productivity across all segments. items.title: Figma, Inc. (FIG) Up 5.2% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?

items.title: CVS Health (CVS) Up 1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?

items.title: Charles River (CRL) Up 10.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Charles River Laboratories (CRL) shares have gained 10.5% since its Q2 2026 earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. However, estimates have been trending downward since the earnings release, and the stock carries weak VGM scores despite maintaining a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: Cencora (COR) Up 3.8% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Cencora reported Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.48, beating consensus estimates by 2.5%, with 12% year-over-year earnings growth. items.title: Kraft Heinz (KHC) Up 1.8% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Kraft Heinz beat Q2 2026 earnings estimates with adjusted EPS of 56 cents versus consensus of 53 cents, but organic sales fell 1.3% year-over-year. items.title: Why Sandisk Stock Rallied Today
items.summary: Sandisk stock surged 8.35% following Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, an open-source AI platform with 18 million users. The rally reflects investor confidence that Nvidia's expanded AI capabilities will drive demand for Sandisk's NAND flash memory chips, which are critical components in AI data centers. items.title: EMCOR Rises 21% Year to Date: Should Investors Buy the Stock Now?
